chunks: And by this chain, from Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), that he said:

A slab was found under the wall of one of the cities, on which it was written: 'I am God, there is no god but Me, and Muhammad is My Prophet. I wonder how one who is certain of death is happy. I wonder how one who is certain of Divine Destiny is sad. I wonder how one who has experienced the world relies on it. I wonder how one who is certain of the Reckoning commits sins!'
ai.seo_question: What are the four things God wonders about regarding human behavior in this hadith?
ai.summary: This inscription, attributed to Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, reflects the Shia theological emphasis on *tadabbur* (contemplation) of the four key realities: death, destiny (*qadar*), the transient nature of the world (*dunya*), and the Day of Judgment (*hisab*). It serves as a practical guide for spiritual equilibrium, urging believers to align their emotional states with their intellectual certainty in divine decree and accountability.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-158 According to the same documentation, on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.),

“A slab was found under the walls of a town on which it was written, ‘I am God. There is no god but Me. Muhammad is My Prophet. I wonder how one who knows he will die is happy. I wonder how one who is certain about Divine Destiny is sad. I wonder how one who knows about the world relies on it. I wonder how one who is certain about the Reckoning commits sins.’”
